newsitem.title: INDIA: India SEBI permits BSE's expansion to 99 centres.
newsitem.headline: India SEBI permits BSE's expansion to 99 centres.

text.p: Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said on Thursday it approved the Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) proposal to expand its on-line trading terminals to 99 centres across India.
"The BSE is free to expand the trading terminals at the 99 centres ...," SEBI said in a note to the BSE.
The BSE would need the Department of Telecommunications' approval for satellite link-up facilities to enable the expansion, traders said.
The new centres are where there are no stock exchanges currently.

These include: Jalandhar, Chandigarh City, Allahabad, Lucknow, Varanasi, Alwar, Udaipur, Jodhpur, Porbandar, Jamnagar, Bhavnagar, Surat, Veraval, Gandhinagar, Anand, Bharuch, Thane, Dombivali, Nasik, Ulhasnagar, Aurangabad, Nagpur, Mapusa, Ujjain, Gwalior, Vizag, Guntur, Calicut, Trivandrum, Udupi, Trichy, Madurai, Erode, Cuttack and Ranchi.
